summary: The note describes the start of the 1948 Arab–Israeli War. On 15 May 1948, the civil war in Palestine became an inter-state conflict after Israel's Declaration of Independence the previous day. Egypt, Jordan and Syria, with Iraqi expeditionary forces, invaded Palestine, and the fighting lasted about 10 months with several truces, mostly on former British Mandate territory.
one_line: The 1948 war that became inter-state when Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Iraq invaded Palestine on 15 May 1948, a day after Israel declared independence.
key_facts: On 15 May 1948, the ongoing civil war transformed into an inter-state conflict between Israel and the Arab states.
The transformation followed the Israeli Declaration of Independence, which was issued the previous day.
A combined invasion by Egypt, Jordan and Syria, together with expeditionary forces from Iraq, entered Palestine.
Jordan had declared privately to Yishuv emissaries on 2 May that it would abide by a decision not to attack the Jewish state.
The invading forces took control of the Arab areas and immediately attacked Israeli forces and several Jewish settlements.
The fighting was interrupted by several truce periods.
The fighting took place mostly on the former territory of the British Mandate.
For a short time, fighting also took place in the Sinai Peninsula.
For a short time, fighting also took place in southern Lebanon.
